about: The Actus contritionis is an individual penitential prayer. It expresses repentance for and detestation of every sin, acknowledges just punishment, and makes the offense against God, the supreme Good worthy of love above all things, the foremost motive of contrition. It ends with a firm resolve, helped by grace, to sin no more and to avoid near occasions of sin.

s01.translation: O my God, with all my heart I repent of all my sins

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)
Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s03.translation: because by sinning, I have deserved not only the punishments justly ordained by you,

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s04.translation: but above all because I have offended you, the supreme Good, worthy to be loved above all things.

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s05.translation: Therefore I firmly resolve, with the help of your grace, henceforth to sin no more

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

s06.translation: and to avoid the near occasions of sin. Amen.

translation_citations.title: Francis X. Lasance, The Catholic Girl's Guide (1906)

w001.function: A vocative opening the direct address to God.

w005.function: A prepositional phrase expressing the wholeness and sincerity of the repentance.

w006.function: An impersonal verb: accusative “me” is the experiencer and genitive “peccatórum” supplies the object of repentance.

w011.function: The pronoun “ea” refers to all the sins in the preceding segment, and enclitic “-que” coordinates the two predicates.

w012.function: A deponent with active meaning, distinguishing detestation of the sins from repentance alone.

w014.function: An ablative gerund expressing the act by which the speaker deserved punishment and offended God.

w016.function: With “non” it anticipates contrasting “sed præsértim” in the next segment.

w019.function: The ablative agent of passive “statútas”. The pronoun refers to God.

w021.function: A passive participle agreeing with “pœnas”. “Iuste” describes the justice of their establishment.

w022.function: A masculine participle of a deponent verb forming the first-person perfect with “sum”.

w028.function: The object of “offéndi”. The following accusatives describe the same God.

w030.function: A substantival adjective in apposition to “te” names God as the supreme Good.

w032.function: A predicate referring to God. The following relative clause states what God is worthy of.

w036.function: The passive second person keeps God as the recipient of love. The subjunctive is selected by “dignum qui”.

w037.function: Introduces the resolution as the consequence of the preceding motives for contrition.

w039.function: Governs an accusative with two future participles: the speaker resolves that he will not sin and will flee occasions.

w040.function: With “grátia tua” forms an ablative absolute expressing the help of God's grace.

w044.function: The fixed phrase “de cétero” marks a prospective boundary: henceforth, from now on.

w045.function: The accusative subject of both dependent future participles. It is the same singular speaker.

w047.function: A masculine future participle in the construction governed by “propóno”. The negation scopes over future sinning.

w048.function: A genitive gerund dependent on “occasiónes”. Enclitic “-que” coordinates this second term with “peccatúrum”.

w050.function: A moral term denoting near occasions, not every remote circumstance in which sin is possible.

w051.function: The second masculine future participle governed by “propóno” and referring to “me”.
